\[
H = e^{-\frac{(\ln(f / f_0))^2}{2 (\ln(\sigma / f_0))^2}}\, e^{-\Delta\theta^2 / 2 \sigma_\theta^2},\quad f_0 = 1 / 8,\ \sigma / f_0 = 0.55
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(f\): The distance from the center of the spectrum in cycles per pixel
- \(f_0\): The center frequency
- \(\sigma / f_0\): The bandwidth ratio
- \(\Delta\theta\): The angle between a frequency and the filter direction
- \(\sigma_\theta\): The angular spread

The radial part is Field's log-Gabor function, a Gaussian of ln(f / f_0). It is 0 at frequency 0 and falls off slowly toward high frequencies. The angular part is Kovesi's Gaussian of the angle Delta theta between a frequency and the filter direction. Here f is the distance from the center of the spectrum in cycles per pixel. The y axis points down, so the direction of a frequency is atan2(-f_y, f_x). With one direction the filter covers one side of the spectrum, so the result is complex. Without a direction the angular part is left out and the result is real.
